assumptions.summary: The supplied review data are treated as reliable and past trends are assumed to extend into the short future.
The forecast series may be irregular, but no causal relation among market developments and no omitted relevant random variable are assumed.
The supplied variables are assumed to represent product satisfaction and the lexicon to contain needed words.
Average sentence sentiment represents review sentiment, and complex negation, derogatory-positive wording, degree combinations and ambiguity are excluded.
Correlation at least 0.3 is treated as useful for screening.
Review age and author-selected component weights represent customer satisfaction.
Monthly aggregation and sparse-start filtering make the series suitable for short-horizon ARIMA.
Inverse date-gap weight represents diminishing mutual influence between reviews.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Duplicate ids, missing/abnormal values and redundant fields are checked product by product.
Reviews shorter than twenty characters are deleted and text punctuation/case are standardized.
The final retained counts are 17,243 pacifier, 10,732 hair-dryer and 1,536 microwave reviews.
Sentences are joined to emotional dictionaries, function words are removed and review sentiment is calculated.
Seven correlated review variables are screened before PCA.
Review age is calculated against 01/01/2016 and CS is min-max normalized.
Daily histories are integrated monthly and sparse early months are filtered.
Date-sorted, product-matched review pairs form time-weighted next-review variables.

source.title: Market data tracking measurement based on sentiment analysis model and ARIMA model

source_quality.summary: All 24 pages were read in physical order and visually reconciled. The source contains a Summary Sheet, a team marketing letter, cleaning counts, lexicon sentiment, PCA-based CR/CS/COM_S, ARIMA forecasts, non-parametric event tests, K-means extreme-review profiles, model evaluation and conclusions.

decisions: which review fields and products to track, how to rank comprehensive satisfaction, how short-horizon ratings and sentiment may change, whether extreme ratings/words coincide with later review behavior, and which product features deserve attention

title: Market data tracking measurement based on sentiment analysis model and ARIMA model
unresolved_questions: The supplied review data are assumed true and reliable without row-level provenance.
Missing, abnormal and duplicate handling is not released as a complete cleaning ledger.
Manual date repair for hair-dryer records is not independently audited.
The less-than-20-character deletion rule can change sentiment composition.
Deleting marketplace, headline and category fields can remove useful confounders.
Review count is not sales volume without exposure correction.
Helpful-vote ratio is not a calibrated review-quality probability.
Five-star concentration may reflect selection and platform exposure.
Word clouds reward frequency and do not establish feature importance.
The lexicon may omit domain words, negation and sarcasm.
Sentence-average sentiment can hide mixed or ordered sentiment.
Degree adverbs and negative words are simplified by the scoring rules.
The emotional dictionary's coverage and weighting are not independently validated.
One worked review cannot establish sentiment accuracy.
The chosen lexicon route is resource-driven, not accuracy-proven.
Correlation threshold 0.3 is a heuristic screening rule.
PCA loadings are data-dependent and sign conventions can change.
Bartlett/KMO evidence does not establish predictive validity.
Three components explain variation but not customer utility.
CR weights are not calibrated to a ground-truth outcome.
The age factor uses a future reference date and a hidden Amazon-algorithm analogy.
Review age may confound product lifecycle, cohort and platform changes.
Min-max normalization is sample-dependent and sensitive to extrema.
COM_S averages buyers without exposure or product-size adjustment.
Top-ten COM_S lists are descriptive rankings, not causal brand effects.
Product success/failure labels are not independently validated.
Verified purchase status is not a truth guarantee.
Vine membership is not shown to cause helpfulness or success.
Monthly aggregation hides day-level shocks and launch-season structure.
Sparse early-month deletion can bias the forecast horizon.
ARIMA stationarity, differencing and order selection are incompletely reported.
ARIMA residual diagnostics and prediction intervals are absent.
September and October forecasts are short-horizon outputs only.
Sentiment forecasts inherit lexicon and aggregation error.
Product-specific forecast direction is not a causal explanation.
J-T p-values do not show that a star rating caused later review activity.
A non-significant sentiment result needs power and sample-size context.
Wilcoxon event windows can confound review timing and exposure.
One-star and five-star events may be selected by unobserved shocks.
K-means cluster labels depend on initialization and scaling.
Cluster centers are profiles, not fraud proof.
The inverse date-gap weight is a heuristic influence law.
Same-day comments receive a special +1 denominator rule without calibration.
The pseudo-code is not a tested implementation or reproducibility package.
Extreme-word lists are hand-selected and incomplete.
NEG/POS flags do not identify fake reviews.
Pearson significance with 29,511 records can coexist with a small coefficient.
Mann-Whitney significance does not identify manipulation mechanisms.
Product-parent grouping may mix variants or catalog changes.
Customer identity fields can contain sparse or non-independent observations.
Star-rating and sentiment relationships are observational associations.
The paper does not report an independent temporal holdout.
The same source history supports ranking, testing and recommendations.
Forecasts do not include external demand, price or platform-algorithm shocks.
The model assumes no relevant random variables affect the time series.
The assumption that the dictionary contains all needed words is strong.
The assumption that reviews have simple logic excludes complex language.
The company letter can sound more certain than the statistical body.
Performance, appearance, price and life actions lack cost and safety analysis.
Recommendation lists lack conversion, margin and reversal criteria.
A tracking suggestion lacks a calibrated intervention threshold.
The conclusion's "powerful tool" language exceeds independent validation.
Model strengths are self-reported and not benchmarked against alternatives.
Lexicon accuracy above 80 percent is not tied to a frozen test split.
PCA information loss and interpretation ambiguity are acknowledged but not quantified.
The 2002-2015 review horizon may not represent current Amazon behavior.
The data may be missing not at random by product, date or review length.
Reference entries and Contents are provenance, not reusable positive prose.
Small formula signs and dense table labels require raster confirmation.
Reusable writing must preserve non-normality, null results, asymmetry and unresolved causal boundaries.

verification.summary: Summary Sheet was read first and preserves cleaning -> sentiment -> PCA satisfaction -> ARIMA -> non-parametric tests -> recommendation.
Literal Introduction was read before later sections and preserves buyer/company roles plus resource-aware lexicon and ARIMA choices.
All 24 physical pages were read and visually reconciled; References remain non-positive language and the team letter is retained.

weaknesses.summary: The supplied review data are assumed true and reliable without row-level provenance.
Missing, abnormal and duplicate handling is not released as a complete cleaning ledger.
Manual date repair for hair-dryer records is not independently audited.
The less-than-20-character deletion rule can change sentiment composition.
Deleting marketplace, headline and category fields can remove useful confounders.
Review count is not sales volume without exposure correction.
Helpful-vote ratio is not a calibrated review-quality probability.
Five-star concentration may reflect selection and platform exposure.
Word clouds reward frequency and do not establish feature importance.
The lexicon may omit domain words, negation and sarcasm.
Sentence-average sentiment can hide mixed or ordered sentiment.
Degree adverbs and negative words are simplified by the scoring rules.
The emotional dictionary's coverage and weighting are not independently validated.
One worked review cannot establish sentiment accuracy.
The chosen lexicon route is resource-driven, not accuracy-proven.
Correlation threshold 0.3 is a heuristic screening rule.
PCA loadings are data-dependent and sign conventions can change.
Bartlett/KMO evidence does not establish predictive validity.
Three components explain variation but not customer utility.
CR weights are not calibrated to a ground-truth outcome.
The age factor uses a future reference date and a hidden Amazon-algorithm analogy.
Review age may confound product lifecycle, cohort and platform changes.
Min-max normalization is sample-dependent and sensitive to extrema.
COM_S averages buyers without exposure or product-size adjustment.
Top-ten COM_S lists are descriptive rankings, not causal brand effects.
Product success/failure labels are not independently validated.
Verified purchase status is not a truth guarantee.
Vine membership is not shown to cause helpfulness or success.
Monthly aggregation hides day-level shocks and launch-season structure.
Sparse early-month deletion can bias the forecast horizon.
ARIMA stationarity, differencing and order selection are incompletely reported.
ARIMA residual diagnostics and prediction intervals are absent.
September and October forecasts are short-horizon outputs only.
Sentiment forecasts inherit lexicon and aggregation error.
Product-specific forecast direction is not a causal explanation.
J-T p-values do not show that a star rating caused later review activity.
A non-significant sentiment result needs power and sample-size context.
Wilcoxon event windows can confound review timing and exposure.
One-star and five-star events may be selected by unobserved shocks.
K-means cluster labels depend on initialization and scaling.
Cluster centers are profiles, not fraud proof.
The inverse date-gap weight is a heuristic influence law.
Same-day comments receive a special +1 denominator rule without calibration.
The pseudo-code is not a tested implementation or reproducibility package.
Extreme-word lists are hand-selected and incomplete.
NEG/POS flags do not identify fake reviews.
Pearson significance with 29,511 records can coexist with a small coefficient.
Mann-Whitney significance does not identify manipulation mechanisms.
Product-parent grouping may mix variants or catalog changes.
Customer identity fields can contain sparse or non-independent observations.
Star-rating and sentiment relationships are observational associations.
The paper does not report an independent temporal holdout.
The same source history supports ranking, testing and recommendations.
Forecasts do not include external demand, price or platform-algorithm shocks.
The model assumes no relevant random variables affect the time series.
The assumption that the dictionary contains all needed words is strong.
The assumption that reviews have simple logic excludes complex language.
The company letter can sound more certain than the statistical body.
Performance, appearance, price and life actions lack cost and safety analysis.
Recommendation lists lack conversion, margin and reversal criteria.
A tracking suggestion lacks a calibrated intervention threshold.
The conclusion's "powerful tool" language exceeds independent validation.
Model strengths are self-reported and not benchmarked against alternatives.
Lexicon accuracy above 80 percent is not tied to a frozen test split.
PCA information loss and interpretation ambiguity are acknowledged but not quantified.
The 2002-2015 review horizon may not represent current Amazon behavior.
The data may be missing not at random by product, date or review length.
Reference entries and Contents are provenance, not reusable positive prose.
Small formula signs and dense table labels require raster confirmation.
Reusable writing must preserve non-normality, null results, asymmetry and unresolved causal boundaries.
